rows.evidence: Q1: Sections 3.3, 6.2.1-6.2.6, Tables 7, 9, 10, 11, 12, Fig. 25 - the bulletin reports its own PRA survey in 10 villages, on-farm trials on 16 and 71 farmers' fields and on-station experiments at PDCSR Modipuram on laser land leveling (water use, water productivity, yield, cost).
rows.notes: The study is a technical bulletin on laser-assisted precision land leveling in the Indo-Gangetic Plains (surface/flood-irrigated rice-wheat). It contains no data, experiment or discussion on subsurface drip irrigation (SSDI) or drip irrigation of any kind; the only mention of drip is a cited remark that laser leveling can raise surface-irrigation efficiency to sprinkler/drip levels. Its own results concern water saving, water productivity, nutrient-use efficiency and yield from laser leveling versus traditional leveling under flood/basin irrigation. Q1 is marginal: the document is partly an overview/extension bulletin, but it does report own survey and field data, so it is treated as primary; this does not affect the profile because Q2 is 'no' for technology mismatch.

rows.evidence: Q1: Sections 3.3, 6.2, Tables 9-12, Fig. 25 - own PRA survey, on-farm trials (16 and 71 farmers' fields) and on-station trials on laser land leveling.
rows.notes: Same technology mismatch: the study evaluates laser land leveling, not SSDI/drip. The closest own result to 'resilience' is the reduced coefficient of variation in yield and water productivity across 71 farmers under laser leveling (Tables 10, 11), but this concerns land leveling under surface irrigation, not drip irrigation with CA, so it does not count as evidence on the claim.

notes: Full text appears complete (abstract through annexure and glossary). The document is an RWC technical bulletin on laser land leveling; it provides no evidence on drip or subsurface drip irrigation, so both rows are rated as technology mismatch at Q2.
